No power-on screen, boot test, or gameplay clip shown; cannot confirm functionality from a static photo.

risks.risk: Console may not power on or may have internal faults (HDMI port, Blu-ray drive, overheating/fan noise typical of older units).
risks.proof: A video clip of the console powering on, showing the PS4 home screen and system settings model number.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working / for-parts condition

risks.risk: Actual model (Pro vs standard PS4) affects value significantly; seller's text claims Pro but photo shows standard Star Wars edition shell.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the rear/bottom serial sticker or the System > Console Information screen showing model number (CUH-7xxx = Pro, CUH-1xxx/2xxx = standard).
risks.if_unproven: priced as standard PS4, not Pro

risks.risk: Controller functionality (stick drift, button response, battery health) cannot be assessed from a photo.
risks.proof: Short video showing both controllers connected and responsive in-game or in system menu.

risks.risk: Included accessories (power cable, HDMI) may not be original or may be damaged; no close-up of cable ends or plug pins.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of power brick label and plug pins, and HDMI connector ends.
risks.if_unproven: priced as generic/replacement accessories, not confirmed original

risks.risk: Storage capacity and internal wear (HDD/SSD) unknown, affecting resale value.
risks.proof: Photo of System Storage screen or rear label showing GB capacity.
risks.if_unproven: priced at base/lowest common capacity for this model

proof_requests: Video of the console powering on to the home screen, showing the System Information model number and storage size.
Close-up photo of the rear port panel and the serial/model sticker (usually on the underside).
Short clip showing both controllers paired and responsive (stick movement, button presses) on screen.
Close-up of the power brick and HDMI cable connectors to confirm they are original/undamaged.
response.reason: The item is clearly a Star Wars-edition PS4 console with two controllers, but the seller's 'PS4 Pro' claim is contradicted by the visible 'PS4' branding and the standard-PS4 shell design, and no functional proof (power-on, controller test) is shown, so it must be priced as a worst-case, unverified-functionality standard PS4 bundle rather than a Pro.
